title: Power BI - 58 Devices Labor Burn Dashboard (in progress)
blurb: End-to-end labor utilization dashboard modeling an A/E firm's FP&A workflow across three MTA contracts. Built a Python script to generate synthetic labor projections and Deltek Vantagepoint exports, reconciled the datasets in Excel via Power Query, and surfaced the output in a Power BI dashboard.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: End-to-end labor utilization dashboard modeling an A/E firm's FP&A workflow across three MTA contracts replacing 58 elevators and escalators. Ingests weekly Vantagepoint Project Labor Exports (real Deltek schema), sub timesheets in intentionally varied formats, and supersession-controlled revisions of the labor projection. Power Query handles date parsing, employee normalization, functional group derivation, and report supersession; light VBA orchestrates refresh and validation. Built with anonymized data — employee names randomized via Python + Faker, Vantagepoint actuals synthesized by a companion script — with real firm names preserved. The generation scripts are themselves deliverables that demonstrate the data structures a production pipeline would consume.

Power Query handles date parsing, employee normalization, functional group derivation, and report supersession; light VBA orchestrates refresh and validation. Built with anonymized data — employee names randomized via Python + Faker, Vantagepoint actuals synthesized by a companion script — with real firm names preserved. objectives.body: Mirror the planned-vs-actual labor reconciliation that an A/E firm performs weekly across multi-contract engagements, including batched Vantagepoint exports and supersession of labor projection revisions.
Use Python with the Faker library to generate anonymized employee rosters and synthesize Vantagepoint actuals so the dashboard exercises the real Deltek schema without exposing client data.
Treat source data as messy by default; centralize cleaning (date parsing, employee normalization, functional grouping, supersession resolution) in Power Query rather than upstream of the load.
Wrap refresh, validation, and reporting handoffs in VBA macros to demonstrate the button-driven workflow an analyst would use day-to-day.

challenges.body: Subcontractors deliver timesheets in varying layouts; reconciling them against a single canonical employee/project key required normalization rules baked into Power Query rather than upstream cleaning.

Revisions of the projection arrive as full new copies, not deltas, so Power Query needs to detect the latest revision and exclude superseded ones from the model — handled with a version-stamped folder layer.

challenges.lead: Synthesized actuals that exercise real failure modes
challenges.body: The Python actuals generator needs to produce data that occasionally violates expected joins (missing employees, off-cycle entries) so the reconciliation layer's edge cases are actually visible in QA.

futureFeatures.body: Finish the visual layer (planned-vs-actual variance, burndown by contract, functional-group heat) and validation page; project is currently mid-Power-Query reconciliation.
Add a drillthrough page that surfaces individual utilization, billable mix, and projection drift to support FP&A's monthly review cadence.
Wire VBA to flag contracts where actuals diverge from projection beyond a configurable threshold, surfacing in the validation step rather than waiting for visual inspection.

title: AI-Assisted Development — Risk Register Revamp using Claude Code
blurb: AI-assisted Power BI dashboard revamp built with Claude Code: phased planning, MCP integration, Test-Driven Development, and a markdown-tracked workflow that compresses token usage and locks decisions between sessions.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: Revamp of a risk dashboard that was initially created by a project controls engineer learning the basic mechanical skills of Power BI. The revamped dashboard utilizes an AI-assisted workflow defined by the learning goals below.
description: Revamp of a risk dashboard that was initially created by a project controls engineer learning the basic mechanical skills of Power BI. The revamped dashboard utilizes an AI-assisted workflow defined by the learning goals below.

objectives.body: Use an AI-assisted workflow to create high-quality dashboards following industry-recommended architecture and visual design.

Follow an AI-assisted workflow that reduces token usage and context bloat through phased planning, explicit assignment of subagents to subtasks, and a project-level markdown file that updates and clears context at the end of every phase.
Connect Claude Code to Power BI via MCP server.
Provide Claude Code with the ability to view its own work. Employ Test-Driven Development with user-generated test requirements at the end of each phase of the project.
Document each challenge and breakthrough in a concise summary, recorded on a markdown file for future project use.

Python scripts emulate real-project risk-log updates, appending to Risk_Updates_Master.xlsx and replacing Risk_Register_Master.xlsx source data. appendupdates.py has guardrails that alert the user to edge cases where an update date exceeds 1½ months from the append date; current master copies are date-stamped on the last update and moved to the archive folder.
Display an interactive version of the dashboard inside the modal view of this technical project on my portfolio website.

challenges.body: The current Power BI Desktop release errored when opening .PBIP files with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.2 or higher installed. Reverting Newtonsoft.Json to 13.0.0 restored PBIP file opening through the desktop app.

Conditional formatting authored via the PBIR CLI did not apply to the visuals. A first attempt restructured the AI-assisted procedure around a helper DAX measure returning the hex code, but the helper measure greyed out as a field choice in the dialog. Final resolution had Claude Code reverse-engineer user-authored fx rules to identify the renderer-engaging shape. The method was applied to every new visual type, with per-visual dependencies (active slot index, selector presence, schema version) recorded in a markdown file to seed a Skill for future Power BI projects.

Claude Code defaulted to user-side verification from the desktop app at every stage gate, which risked version overwrites (user saves after agent edits) and added user friction. The agent was instructed to publish and refresh through Microsoft Fabric CLI in the browser instead, reducing user effort, time per project, and the chance of version-control conflicts.

Turnover files from the original manually-built dashboard carried design intent that was deliberately changed or removed during the revamp's planning phase. A custom Skill was authored that prompts Claude Code to replace irrelevant context in the project's CLAUDE.md, keeping the agent aligned with the revamp's current design decisions.

The drillthrough page's Mitigations visual showed a single concatenated string of updates and dates, reading as a sloppy block. A new measure pulls individual risk updates from Risk_Updates to replace the static-column lookup, sorted latest-first with line breaks between entries.

futureFeatures.body: Add seed data for multiple contracts and enable program-level rollups. Repurposing the existing dashboard requires a project dimension with multiple rows, project slicers on every page, and a careful review of which measures need re-aggregation across projects.

Pair the qualitative P×I matrix with quantitative methods (expected value, Monte Carlo on contingency). The current build is qualitative screening only; the quantitative work will be a separate project.

title: Power BI - Risk Register Dashboard
blurb: Construction risk register dashboard built around a Python update pipeline: dated entries written into the source Excel register are parsed and appended to a separate update table that powers the dashboard's trend and history visuals.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: Power BI risk register dashboard for a single-contract bridge and utility relocation project, built on PMBOK qualitative risk screening — a 5×5 probability-impact matrix using P × MAX(C,S) scoring with Low / Medium / High banding. The data architecture separates the register (the human-edit surface) from a Risk_Updates flat table (the time-series source), joined many-to-one on a stable risk_id key. A companion Python script handles append-only propagation — parsing new dated entries from the register's mitigation_log column and appending them as rows to Risk_Updates with year inference via a documented month rule. Power BI refreshes off both files via direct file connections; script appends flow through without manual remodeling. Built with synthetic data designed to exercise every visual, not represent real project record.

Built with synthetic data designed to exercise every visual, not represent real project record.

objectives.lead: Separation of edit surface and time-series source
objectives.body: Keep the register as the human-friendly edit layer and route history into a separate Risk_Updates flat table joined on a stable risk_id, avoiding the trap of growing a single sheet into both roles.
Parse mitigation_log entries with year inference and append to Risk_Updates without rewriting history; month-rule edge cases are documented in the script.

Implement the 5×5 P × I matrix with P × MAX(C,S) scoring and Low/Medium/High banding such that the matrix renders all 25 cells including empties — which requires a disconnected axis table, not just the data.

objectives.lead: New DAX patterns for trend & heat
objectives.body: Author AVERAGEX with RELATED for the average-score trend across a to-one relationship without invoking bidirectional cross-filter, plus a single P × I cell-score measure shared across cost-impact, schedule-impact, and max-impact matrix variants.

challenges.lead: Forcing matrix cells to render including empties
challenges.body: Default Power BI suppresses zero-count cells, breaking the 5×5 layout. Resolved with a disconnected axis table and a SELECTEDVALUE-driven count measure so every cell paints whether or not risks fall in it.

challenges.lead: Avoiding the bidirectional cross-filter trap on trend
challenges.body: The average-score trend across the to-one Risk_Updates relationship initially called for bidirectional filtering, which would have corrupted unrelated measures. Resolved with AVERAGEX + RELATED to compute through the existing single-direction relationship.

Page 1 visuals all scope to mitigation_status = active, but the resolved-count tile on the same page needed to ignore that filter. Resolved with a CALCULATE override on the count measure rather than splitting the page.

challenges.lead: Year inference on parsed mitigation_log entries
challenges.body: Free-text dated entries in the register lack explicit years; the Python parser uses a documented month rule with edge-case warnings rather than guessing silently.

futureFeatures.body: A revamp of this dashboard using Claude Code and an MCP-driven workflow is a separate project on this site (Risk Register Revamp); it carries forward the data architecture decisions and re-authors the visuals through the PBIR CLI.
Pair the qualitative P × I matrix with quantitative methods (expected value, Monte Carlo on contingency). The current build is qualitative screening only.

title: Power BI - Agency Contingent Employee Staffing Tracker
blurb: A reporting tool built to manage a contingent staffing program placing personnel into agency roles.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: A Power BI reporting tool for a contingent staffing program. It tracks candidates from application through placement and surfaces hiring pipeline, interview scoring, and margin on each placement. The model is four tables — roles, candidates, interviews, and status history — with Excel kept as the data entry layer so all calculations stay in Power BI. The headline ranking metric was reworked late in the build from interview score to gross margin per placement, which forced modeling of bill rate against pay rate.
description: A Power BI reporting tool for a contingent staffing program. It tracks candidates from application through placement and surfaces hiring pipeline, interview scoring, and margin on each placement. The model is four tables — roles, candidates, interviews, and status history — with Excel kept as the data entry layer so all calculations stay in Power BI. The headline ranking metric was reworked late in the build from interview score to gross margin per placement, which forced modeling of bill rate against pay rate.

objectives.lead: Four-table relational model in Power BI
objectives.body: Keep roles, candidates, interviews, and status history as separate fact/dim tables joined on stable keys, with Excel as the edit layer and DAX as the calculation layer.

objectives.lead: Sort-order columns in Power Query, not DAX
objectives.body: Build numeric sort keys for pipeline stage as Power Query conditional columns so they're computed before the data model loads, sidestepping DAX calculated-column circular dependencies.
Pull role fields through each candidate's own role ID (not directly from the Roles table) and lock the Candidates→Interviews relationship to a single direction to prevent fan-out.
Model bill rate against pay rate so the placement ranking reflects gross margin rather than interview score — a more decision-useful metric for the program owner.

challenges.lead: Circular dependency on DAX sort key
challenges.body: Building the pipeline sort key as a DAX calculated column triggered a circular dependency. Resolved by moving the sort key into Power Query as a conditional column, which evaluates before the data model loads.

The candidate table showed each candidate against every role because role fields were being pulled straight from the Roles table and two competing relationship paths existed. Resolved by looking up role fields via each candidate's own role ID and correcting cross-filter direction on Candidates→Interviews.

challenges.lead: Late metric pivot from interview score to gross margin
challenges.body: Switching the ranking metric mid-build meant adding bill rate and pay rate to the model and reworking the headline table — a deliberate exercise in the cost of late metric changes versus locking metrics up front.

futureFeatures.body: The status history table is in the model but not yet visualized; add average cycle time per stage and bottleneck detection to the program-owner view.
Now that gross margin is modeled at the placement level, roll it up by recruiter to support compensation and coaching conversations.

title: Full Stack Web Development - Weave
blurb: A travel planning tool built to demonstrate the ability to deploy a full-stack application. Additional features include the integration of google maps API and nodemailer.
label: WEB DEVELOPMENT
detail: Weave is a MERN-stack group trip planning app developed and launched in one week. It pairs a Node + Express backend with a MongoDB NoSQL database. Users search businesses and points of interest via Google Places autocomplete and pin them onto an interactive map, building a shared itinerary across the group.
description: Weave is a MERN-stack group trip planning app developed and launched in one week. It pairs a Node + Express backend with a MongoDB NoSQL database. Users search businesses and points of interest via Google Places autocomplete and pin them onto an interactive map, building a shared itinerary across the group.

objectives.body: Ship a working MERN app — frontend, API, database, and hosting — end-to-end in a single sprint, prioritizing deploy-readiness over feature breadth.
Wire Google Places (autocomplete + map rendering) and Nodemailer into a single coherent UX where search, pin, and notify all feed the same itinerary state.
Use React-Redux to keep the shared itinerary in sync across multiple users' views without round-tripping through the backend on every interaction.

objectives.lead: NoSQL document modeling for trip data
objectives.body: Model trips, members, and pinned POIs as nested documents in MongoDB rather than relational tables, leaning on the document model for the natural shape of itinerary data.

challenges.body: Sprint-specific challenges (deployment quirks, API quota handling, real-time itinerary sync edge cases) are not yet documented here. The project was built in a one-week sprint and challenges were resolved on the fly without a retrospective.

futureFeatures.body: Weave was built as a learning sprint rather than an ongoing product; no feature roadmap has been defined. Likely directions if revisited: persistent user accounts, mobile-responsive itinerary view, and an export-to-calendar flow.

title: JavaScript + D3.js Single Page Application - Projectify
blurb: Rough order of magnitude estimate single page web application for Medical Office Fit-outs
label: WEB DEVELOPMENT
detail: A data visualization tool that helps commercial building owners and prospective tenants forecast tenant fit-out costs at the concept stage, before design documents are available. Users input square footage and select a construction type to generate rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) projections driven by $/SF benchmarks compiled from completed medical office fit-outs. Results render on an interactive D3.js bar chart that supports real-time scope adjustment, giving stakeholders immediate visibility into cost drivers and value-engineering opportunities. The tool applies core project controls principles — historical benchmarking, parametric estimating, and visual reporting — to early-stage feasibility decisions where cost certainty is lowest and the impact of scope choices is highest.

objectives.body: Compile $/SF benchmarks from completed medical-office fit-outs and expose them as live inputs so feasibility-stage estimates respond to scope changes in real time.
Render the ROM as an interactive bar chart where scope dials drive the chart directly, surfacing the dominant cost drivers without requiring spreadsheet literacy.
Build the app as a vanilla SPA (JavaScript + D3) rather than React, to learn the underlying state and rendering primitives that frameworks abstract away.

objectives.lead: Project controls principles for early-stage estimating
objectives.body: Apply historical benchmarking, parametric estimating, and visual reporting at the feasibility stage where cost certainty is lowest and scope decisions have the highest leverage.

challenges.body: Detailed notes on D3.js scale handling, benchmark normalization across mixed-source fit-outs, and SPA state management without a framework are not yet documented here.

futureFeatures.body: Projectify was built as a learning exercise rather than a maintained product; no formal roadmap exists. Likely directions if revisited: expanded fit-out type library (lab, classroom, retail), confidence-interval bands on the ROM, and exportable estimate summaries.
